h.select_rule: Discard any hypothesis whose condition is the edited field's own current value, or whose condition merely disables or disconnects the edited component. From the rest, keep 10 with distinct mechanisms and field pairs, favouring those where an informed expert could plausibly bet on either direction.
h.strategy: Two patterns are banned because experts find them obvious: (1) conditioning on the current value of the same field being edited, which just restates that upgrading a weak setting helps more than upgrading a strong one; (2) conditions that make the edited component unused, unreachable or inert. Instead, each hypothesis must link two DIFFERENT fields that interact through a non-trivial mechanism, such as substitution between parallel routes, a capacity already supplied elsewhere, one part acting as a bottleneck for another, or interference that turns a usually helpful edit harmful. No condition setting may appear in more than two hypotheses. Use the gaps and negated assumptions as the source of each idea. In each 'why', name the mechanism and explain why the opposite direction is also a priori plausible.

hyps.why: A direct 0->3 conv summed with an existing 1->3 conv adds largely redundant capacity at the output node, so its gain shrinks.
Without a direct 0->3 path, the output relies more on the 2->3 edge, so making it a learned conv yields a larger gain.
A residual 0->3 identity eases optimisation of the deeper conv path that a conv on edge 0 creates, so that conv helps more.
With 0->2 removed, a pooled 1->2 edge becomes node 2's sole input and forces everything downstream through a parameter-free blur.
An identity 0->3 beside a conv into the output forms a ResNet-style residual block that stabilises training of the stacked network.
If 2->3 is already an identity, a second identity into node 3 overweights unprocessed features and adds little gradient-path benefit.
Without a direct 0->3 edge, a skip on 2->3 supplies the short path to the output that otherwise is missing.
With the direct path already a learned conv, a 1->3 identity adds a complementary residual-like route instead of competing for the conv role.
When node 2 receives only pooled features from node 1, a 1x1 on 2->3 cannot add the learned spatial filtering that path lacks, so the edit is worse.
Deleting the direct 0->3 edge when 2->3 is also absent leaves node 3 dependent on a single edge, so the removal hurts much more.
